item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00159","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C21","C22","C16"],"selected_candidate_label":"C21","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C21 is a highly plausible direct template. Just two days earlier, it used the same two-stage machinery: the Acting Secretary of the Interior adopts and submits a geographically described closed-area regulation under the Migratory Bird Treaty Act, Reorganization Plan II, the two bird conventions, and the Administrative Procedure Act; the President then finds that the regulation effectuates the Act and approves and proclaims it. The child closely repeats distinctive language governing the designated area's effective date and prohibited conduct, adapting principally the location and boundary description and adding provisions superseding the prior Oregon regulation. C22 shares much of the same statutory approval framework but concerns general migratory-bird regulations rather than designation of a closed area.
